subject: physics
question_text: Compare the bulk modulus of solids, liquids and gases.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya *IPE Study Material for Jr. Students* 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 9 Very Short Answer Question 9 (printed p.98). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: bulk modulus decreases in the order solid > liquid > gas because intermolecular spacing increases in that order, so the fractional volume change for a given pressure change is smallest in solids and largest in gases.

insider_note: The order alone is only half the answer — the examiner looks for a reason connecting molecular spacing to the resistance to compression for the second step.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Order of bulk modulus
lines: The bulk modulus decreases in the order
steps.margin_note: The order must be stated as solid > liquid > gas, not just described in words, to earn this mark cleanly.
steps.why: Bulk modulus B = −ΔP/(ΔV/V) measures resistance to compression; the closer the molecules, the smaller the fractional volume change for the same pressure change, so B is largest for solids.
common_mistakes: Writing the order the wrong way round (gas > liquid > solid).
Comparing Young's modulus instead of bulk modulus.
steps.memory_tip: For the same increase in pressure the solid's volume changes least and the gas's changes most.

steps.label: Reason
lines: A solid resists a change in volume the
most because its molecules are held
tightly together; a gas resists least
because its molecules are far apart.
steps.margin_note: State a reason connected to molecular spacing — restating the order in different words does not earn this mark.
steps.why: The reasoning ties the order to the molecular picture: tightly packed molecules in a solid resist coming closer under pressure, while widely spaced gas molecules move closer easily.
common_mistakes: Giving no reason at all, only the order.
Saying gases are 'weaker' instead of explaining the spacing between molecules.
steps.memory_tip: Widely spaced gas molecules move closer under a small pressure change.
